name: Standard Big-Tech 5-Pillar System Design Rubric
description: Industry-standard evaluation framework assessing candidates across requirements gathering, architectural structure, data storage design, resilience and fault tolerance, and communication with trade-off justification.

criteria.title: Scope Boundary & Requirement Decomposition
criteria.description: Ability to proactively distinguish functional vs. non-functional requirements, clarify ambiguous assumptions, define SLA/SLO boundaries, and estimate capacity constraints.

level_expectations.junior: Relies heavily on interviewer prompts; may jump prematurely into database tables without clarifying scale, traffic patterns, or core constraints.
level_expectations.mid: Identifies primary functional requirements and asks standard non-functional questions (e.g., QPS, latency, availability); performs rough math with guidance.
level_expectations.senior: Proactively establishes system boundaries, explicit SLAs (e.g., 99.99% availability, P99 < 50ms), and drives back-of-the-envelope estimations with clear formulas.
level_expectations.staff: Frames requirements within business impact and organizational constraints; defines failure blast radius, multi-region regulatory compliance, and budget limits early.
level_expectations.principal: Challenges foundational assumptions; reframes the core business problem; identifies cost-value inflection points and enterprise ecosystem dependencies.

criteria.title: Component Architecture & End-to-End Data Flow
criteria.description: Ability to lay out clean client-server topologies, define microservice boundaries, establish robust API contracts, and trace synchronous/asynchronous data workflows.

level_expectations.junior: Draws monolithic or overly simplified boxes without clear API definitions, protocol selection, or transport awareness.
level_expectations.mid: Designs basic tiered architecture (Clients -> Load Balancer -> Web App -> DB); defines standard REST endpoints with reasonable separation of concerns.
level_expectations.senior: Architects clean distributed services; designs decoupled event-driven workflows with queues/pub-sub; specifies clear API schemas and idempotent contracts.
level_expectations.staff: Optimizes system-wide topology for team ownership, blast radius containment, multi-datacenter traffic routing, and edge computing offload.
level_expectations.principal: Designs modular, evolvable architectures; models complex distributed protocols and multi-tier edge-to-core ingestion fabrics.

criteria.title: Data Modeling, Storage Engines & Partitioning Strategy
criteria.description: Ability to select optimal storage paradigms (SQL, NoSQL, TSDB, Blob), design relational/document schemas, define sharding/partition keys, and design multi-tiered caching.

level_expectations.junior: Defaults to a single relational DB table without indexing thoughts; treats caching as a magic bullet without eviction strategies.
level_expectations.mid: Chooses appropriate SQL vs NoSQL models; outlines basic database schemas and foreign keys; incorporates Redis with standard TTL expiration.
level_expectations.senior: Justifies storage engine choices based on read/write access patterns; designs sharding schemes with composite partition keys; handles cache stampedes and cache invalidation.
level_expectations.staff: Deeply analyzes consistency models (PACELC / CAP theorem); designs customized LSM-tree vs B-Tree tradeoffs, distributed consensus, and cross-datacenter replication topologies.
level_expectations.principal: Innovates specialized hybrid storage architectures; balances hardware mechanical sympathy (IOPS, NVMe, memory bus) against cloud cost economics at planetary scale.

criteria.title: Fault Tolerance, Failure Modes & Observability
criteria.description: Ability to identify single points of failure (SPOFs), implement resilience mechanisms (circuit breakers, retries with jitter, backpressure), and design comprehensive observability.

level_expectations.junior: Rarely considers server crashes, network partitions, or cascading timeouts unless prompted.
level_expectations.mid: Identifies primary SPOFs (e.g., single DB instance); adds database read replicas and basic health checks.
level_expectations.senior: Designs comprehensive defense-in-depth: rate limiting, circuit breakers, exponential backoff with jitter, graceful degradation, and structured distributed tracing.
level_expectations.staff: Designs self-healing systems; prepares for catastrophic region-wide failovers, split-brain scenarios, thundering herds, and data reconciliation pipelines.
level_expectations.principal: Defines global disaster recovery SLAs (RTO/RPO); designs chaos engineering strategies and automated canary verification across sovereign cloud regions.

criteria.title: Collaborative Communication & Trade-Off Articulation
criteria.description: Ability to drive structured discussions, communicate technical reasoning transparently, actively listen to interviewer hints, and evaluate multi-dimensional architectural trade-offs.

level_expectations.junior: Struggles to articulate thought process; gets defensive or stuck on minor implementation details without addressing big picture.
level_expectations.mid: Communicates clearly; responds well to hints and questions; explains basic pros/cons of selected technologies.
level_expectations.senior: Leads the conversation proactively with structure; explicitly presents multiple solutions and rigorously compares latency, cost, and complexity tradeoffs.
level_expectations.staff: Communicates with executive-level clarity; synthesizes complex distributed dilemmas into crisp decisions; demonstrates high emotional intelligence and pedagogical leadership.
level_expectations.principal: Inspires architectural confidence; articulates strategic industry paradigms; aligns engineering excellence with organizational and business priorities.
